the night of Erev Rosh Hashanah 5733

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Gemara's decree that when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, the shofar is not blown outside the Temple, because the pleasure of Shabbat itself supersedes the need to awaken pleasure through shofar, except in the Temple where a higher pleasure is drawn.

translations.translation: On Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, in the Temple they would blow [the shofar], but not in the rest of the country.
And it is explained in the Gemara
that it is the Rabbis who decreed regarding it,
for all are obligated in the shofar blast, but not all are expert in the shofar blast,
a decree lest one take it in his hand and go to an expert to learn, and carry it four cubits in the public domain.
And the precise point in this is known,
why did the Sages see fit to set aside a positive Torah commandment,
and especially the mitzvah of shofar, which is a very lofty and exalted mitzvah,
because of a mere decree
[and especially nowadays,
when there is no public domain by Torah law,
and the decree lest he carry it is only so that he not come to a Rabbinic prohibition].
And also,
the concern is for the common and light-minded people,
and how did they prevent the mitzvah for many great and good tzaddikim because of this?
And the explanation is known,
that this [need] to blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is in order to thereby awaken above the pleasure in the creation of the worlds,
and since on Shabbat, in its own right, there is [already] the pleasure,
therefore,
on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, the mitzvah of shofar blast is not so strongly in force
(with all the stir)
as on Rosh Hashanah that falls on a weekday,
and therefore it is set aside because of the concern lest he carry it four cubits in the public domain.
And that in the Temple they would blow even on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat,
it is,
because in pleasure there are several levels,
and the level of pleasure that they drew through the shofar blast in the Temple is more elevated than the level of pleasure of Shabbat.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, the pleasure comes from Shabbat itself rather than from human effort, seemingly lacking the superior quality of pleasure drawn through the service of Israel, though the recitation of Shofar verses provides the revelation of that pleasure.

translations.translation: B)
And one must understand,
for it is known
that this [need] to awaken the pleasure on Rosh Hashanah through the service of man
(the shofar blast),
even though at the beginning of creation the drawing down was by itself,
it is,
because through the arousal of the pleasure above
(now)
being through the service of Israel,
whose root is in the Awtsmoos,
the pleasure that is drawn now is more elevated than the pleasure drawn on its own accord
(at the beginning of creation).
Based on this,
on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat,
where the pleasure is from the aspect of the time of Shabbat
(Shabbat is sanctified and stands [on its own]),
it seemingly lacks the superiority of the pleasure that is awakened through the service of man.
And even though on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat there is also the service of reciting the Shofar verses,
the recitation of the verses is so that the drawing down will be in revelation.
And as explained in the continuation of “Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah” 5666,
the drawing down through the mitzvos is not so much in revelation,
and the revelation is through the Torah,
“Torah is light.”
Therefore,
in order that the drawing down of pleasure through the fulfillment of the mitzvah of shofar blast be in revelation, it is through the recitation of the Shofar verses.
And this is the reason that even on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat we recite the Shofar verses,
even though the drawing down of pleasure then is on its own accord,
for the drawing down from Shabbat itself is above,
and in order for there to be revelation below it is through the recitation of the Shofar verses.
And since through the recitation of the verses it is only the revelation of the drawing down,
and the drawing down itself is from Shabbat itself,
therefore, on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, it seemingly lacks the superiority that is made through service.
